answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn reputation or receive work, then slash that stake when independently verified fraud is proven. A pulse of small, randomized audits makes it risky to split one attacker across a vine of fresh accounts: each account must tie up capital and survive scrutiny, while failure destroys the bond. In a tundra of low-trust newcomers, this turns cheap identity creation into costly, detectable exposure—not an absolute guarantee against Sybils.
